'''Leandro Mateus Barbosa''' ({{IPA|pt|leˈɐ̃dɾu baʁˈbozɐ}}; born November 28, 1982),<ref name="Curr Bio">{{cite book|title=Current Biography Yearbook 2011|year=2011|publisher=H.W. Wilson|location=Ipswich, MA|isbn=9780824211219|pages=[https://archive.org/details/currentbiography0000unse_z0h6/page/44 44–47]|chapter=Barbosa, Leandro|chapter-url=https://archive.org/details/currentbiography0000unse_z0h6/page/44}}</ref> also known as '''Leandrinho Barbosa''', is a Brazilian former professional [[basketball]] player who is an assistant coach for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news-blogs/leandro-barbosa-20200914|title=Warriors Name Leandro Barbosa Player Mentor Coach 14-Year NBA Veteran & 2015 NBA Champion Joins Head Coach Steve Kerr's Staff|date=September 14, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 14, 2020}}</ref> He also represented the senior [[Brazilian national basketball team]]. Barbosa previously won the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award]], with the Suns in 2007, and an [[NBA championship]] with the Warriors in 2015. In Brazil, he is also commonly known by his nickname "Leandrinho" ("Little Leandro") Barbosa,<ref name="nba.com">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2003/profiles/BarbosaLeandrinho.html |title=Prospect Profile: Leandrinho Barbosa. |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=August 5, 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412111644/https://www.nba.com/draft2003/profiles/BarbosaLeandrinho.html |archive-date=April 12, 2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and in the United States, Barbosa was nicknamed "'''the Brazilian Blur'''", referring to his playing speed.<ref name="sixthman">[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2846672 Barbosa runs away with Sixth Man Award], published April 23, 2007</ref> At a height of {{convert|1.92|m|ftin|frac=4|abbr=on}} tall,<ref name="lnb.com.br">[https://lnb.com.br/atletas/leandro-mateus-barbosa/ Leandrinho Leandro Mateus Barbosa Posição Ala/Armador Altura / Peso 1.92 / 91kg {{in lang|pt}}.]</ref> Barbosa played at the [[shooting guard]] position.

==Early career==
Barbosa started his career with [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras (basketball)|Palmeiras]] when he was 17. Barbosa played in the regional [[São Paulo State Basketball Championship|São Paulo State Championship]], under the command of [[Lula Ferreira]], who went on to become the senior [[Brazilian national basketball team|Brazilian national team]]'s head coach.<ref name=brbio>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/brasil/perfil_barbosa_030622.html|title=Perfil: Leandrinho Barbosa|publisher=NBA Brasil|language=pt|access-date=December 6, 2010}}</ref>

At age 19, while playing in the regional São Paulo State Championship with [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]], Barbosa averaged 14.2 points per game. After that, he was traded to the Brazilian club [[Associação Bauru Basketball Team|Bauru]], in January 2001.<ref name=brbio/>

During his first season as a professional in Brazil, while playing with Tilibra/Bauru, Barbosa was coached by [[Jorge "Guerrinha" Guerra]]. He averaged 15.8 points, 6.4 assists, and 1.7 steals per game. Barbosa was named the São Paulo State Championship's 2001 Rookie of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fpb.com.br/_dynamics/melhoresdoano/melhores2001.asp|title=Melhores do Ano 2001 – Troféu Oswaldo Caviglia|publisher=Federação Paulista de Basquete|language=pt|access-date=December 6, 2010|archive-date=October 7, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101007191551/http://www.fpb.com.br/_dynamics/melhoresdoano/melhores2001.asp|url-status=dead}}</ref> He ended the season as the regional competition's fourth-ranked player in three-point field goal percentage, sixth in assists, and 11th in field goals.<ref name=brbio/> In 2002, Barbosa won Brazil's top-tier level league, the [[Brazilian Basketball Championship|Brazilian Championship]], as a member of Bauru. He was also selected to the senior Brazilian national team and played at the [[2002 FIBA World Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbb.com.br/atletas_tecnicos/atleta_tecnico.asp?cod=897&tipo=&msb=1|publisher=[[Brazilian Basketball Confederation|CBB]]|title=Leandrinho|access-date=December 6, 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120122161705/http://www.cbb.com.br/atletas_tecnicos/atleta_tecnico.asp?cod=897&tipo=&msb=1|archive-date=January 22, 2012|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Phoenix Suns (2003–2010)===
Standing at {{convert|6|ft|3|in}} and possessing a {{convert|6|ft|10|in|adj=on|m}} [[wingspan]], Barbosa was selected 28th overall in the [[2003 NBA draft]] by the [[San Antonio Spurs]], but his rights were acquired by the Suns in a trade for a future protected first-round draft pick.

Barbosa holds the Suns franchise record for points scored in a game by a rookie as a first-time starter, with 27 against the [[Chicago Bulls]] on January 5, 2004.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/leandro_barbosa/bio.html|title=Leandro Barbosa: Bio|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 6, 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101202212845/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/leandro_barbosa/bio.html|archive-date=December 2, 2010|df=mdy-all}}</ref> He set the Suns' record for three-point field goals by a rookie in consecutive games after hitting at least one three-pointer per game during a 10-game streak from January 2 to 19.<ref name=bio/>

During the 2006–07 season, Barbosa averaged 18.1 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 4.0 assists in 32.7 minutes per game despite playing off the bench.<ref name=profile>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/leandro_barbosa/index.html|title=Leandro Barbosa Info Page|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 6, 2010}}</ref> He was also the recipient of the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07]] [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award]].<ref name="sixthman" />[[File:Suns on offense at Phoenix at Golden State 3-15-09 2.JPG|thumb|Barbosa (#10) shooting in March 2009|left]]

Barbosa scored a career-high of 41 points in a 140–118 victory over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on February 20, 2009. He also had seven rebounds, seven assists, and six steals.

===Toronto Raptors (2010–2012)===
On July 14, 2010, Barbosa was traded along with [[Dwayne Jones (basketball)|Dwayne Jones]] to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[Hedo Türkoğlu]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/barbosa_trade_071410.html |title=Raptors Acquire Barbosa And Jones From Phoenix|work=NBA.com |date=July 14, 2010 |access-date=February 22, 2013}}</ref>

On August 18, 2011, Barbosa signed with [[Flamengo Basketball]] of Brazil for the duration of the [[2011 NBA lockout]]. His deal had an out-clause that would allow him to return to the NBA once the lockout ended.<ref>Wolstat, Ryan. (August 18, 2011) [http://www.torontosun.com/2011/08/18/barbosa-heads-back-to-brazil Barbosa heads back to Brazil]. torontosun.com. Retrieved August 10, 2016.</ref> With the lockout concluding in December 2011, Barbosa returned to the Raptors.

===Indiana Pacers (2012)===
On March 15, 2012, Barbosa was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] for a future second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers_acquire_barbosa_from_raptors_2012_03_15.html |title=Pacers acquire Barbosa from Raptors|work=NBA.com |date=March 15, 2012 |access-date=February 22, 2013}}</ref> With the help of Barbosa, Indiana improved significantly enough to make it to the second round of the playoffs before losing to the [[Miami Heat]].

===Boston Celtics (2012–2013)===
On October 18, 2012, Barbosa signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-sign-leandro-barbosa |title=Celtics sign guard Barbosa|work=NBA.com |date=October 18, 2012 |access-date=February 22, 2013}}</ref>

On February 12, 2013, after a game against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] on February 11, it was confirmed that Barbosa tore his ACL, prematurely ending his season.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/leandro-barbosa-injury-update Leandro Barbosa Injury Update]. NBA.com (February 12, 2013). Retrieved August 10, 2016.</ref> Barbosa was the third member of the team whose injury ended his season early in a span of three weeks, joining [[Rajon Rondo]] and [[Jared Sullinger]].{{citation needed|date=July 2013}}

===Washington Wizards (2013)===
On February 21, 2013, Barbosa and [[Jason Collins]] were traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Jordan Crawford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-acquire-collins-and-barbosa-boston |title=Wizards Acquire Collins and Barbosa From Boston |work=NBA.com |date=February 21, 2013 |access-date=February 22, 2013}}</ref> Despite being on the team during that time, he never played for the Wizards in the process.

===Esporte Clube Pinheiros (2013–2014)===
On November 19, 2013, Barbosa signed with the [[Esporte Clube Pinheiros (basketball)|Esporte Clube Pinheiros]] of Brazil for the 2013–14 season. During this time, he averaged over 20 points, three rebounds, and three assists for the team. In January 2014, Barbosa returned to the United States to play in the NBA once again.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20140106033752/http://www.jornalacidade.com.br/esportes/NOT,0,492,913691,Leandrinho+deixa+Pinheiros+para+acertar+volta+para+NBA.aspx Leandrinho deixa Pinheiros para acertar volta para NBA]. Jornalacidade.com.br (January 5, 2014). Retrieved August 10, 2016.</ref>

===Return to Phoenix (2014)===
On January 8, 2014, Barbosa signed a 10-day contract with the Phoenix Suns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-leandro-barbosa|title=Suns Sign Leandro Barbosa|work=NBA.com|date=January 8, 2014|access-date=January 8, 2014}}</ref> He would immediately play for the Suns in a narrow 104–103 victory over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. Barbosa would have his best night during the first 10-day contract on January 13 against the [[New York Knicks]] when he scored 21 points, marking his first 20+ point game since 2012, back when he played for the Celtics. However, Barbosa would have a right shoulder strain after the game.

On January 18, Barbosa signed a second 10-day contract with the Suns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-barbosa-second-10-day-contract|title=Suns Sign Barbosa to Second 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=January 18, 2014|access-date=January 18, 2014}}</ref> He made his first home debut with the Suns in over four years the next day in a 117–103 victory over the [[Denver Nuggets]]. During his second 10-day contract, Barbosa's best performance came on January 24 at home against the [[Washington Wizards]], where he scored 10 points against them.

On January 28, 2014, following the Suns' road game against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], which subsequently marked the end of his second 10-day contract, the Suns liked Barbosa's production for the team, and they decided to sign him for the rest of the [[2013–14 NBA season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/suns-sign-barbosa-remainder-season|title=Suns Sign Barbosa for Remainder of Season|work=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2014|access-date=January 28, 2014}}</ref> On March 4, in a game against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] at home, Barbosa fractured his right hand and missed the rest of the season as a result.

===Golden State Warriors (2014–2016)===
[[File:Leandro Barbosa in 2015.jpg|thumb|upright|Barbosa in 2015]]
On September 10, 2014, Barbosa signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]] following his great performance at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors Sign Leandro Barbosa to Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/barbosa-signing-20140910|access-date=September 11, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=September 10, 2014}}</ref> On December 30, Barbosa scored a season-high 17 points in a 126–86 victory over the Philadelphia 76ers.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400578766 Warriors keep rolling, topple 76ers 126–86]. espn.go.com (December 31, 2014). Retrieved August 10, 2016.</ref> He won his first NBA championship with the Warriors after they defeated the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the [[2015 NBA Finals]] in six games.

On July 13, 2015, Barbosa re-signed with the Warriors.<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors Re-Sign Free Agent Guard Leandro Barbosa|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/barbosa-resign-20150713|access-date=July 13, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2015}}</ref> In [[2015–16 NBA season|2015–16]], he helped the Warriors win an NBA record 73 games to eclipse the 72 wins set by the [[1995–96 Chicago Bulls season|1995–96 Chicago Bulls]]. The Warriors made it to the [[2016 NBA Finals]] after overcoming a 3–1 loss against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in the Western Conference Finals. In Game 1 of the NBA Finals against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on June 2, Barbosa returned from a minor back injury to score 11 points on 5-of-5 shooting off the bench during a 104–89 victory.<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors' supporting cast leads Game 1 NBA Finals win|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160602/CLEGSW/gameinfo.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160603100145/http://www.nba.com/games/20160602/CLEGSW/gameinfo.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 3, 2016|access-date=June 2, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=June 2, 2016}}</ref> However, the Warriors eventually lost in seven games despite a 3–1 lead.

===Third stint with Phoenix (2016–2017)===
On July 19, 2016, Barbosa signed a multi-year deal with the [[Phoenix Suns]], returning to the franchise for a third stint just weeks before playing for his home nation at the [[2016 Summer Olympics]] in [[Rio de Janeiro]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-leandro-barbosa-multiyear-deal|title=Suns Sign Leandro Barbosa|work=NBA.com|date=July 19, 2016|access-date=July 19, 2016}}</ref>

On December 9, Barbosa scored a season-high 21 points and hit five three-pointers in a 119–115 victory over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/barbole01/gamelog/2017/|title=Leandro Barbosa 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 10, 2016}}</ref> On December 28, in a loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]], Barbosa played his 517th game with the Suns, moving him past [[Amar'e Stoudemire]] to 10th on the Suns' all-time games played list.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/gamenotes/suns.pdf |title=Suns Game Notes |work=NBA.com |access-date=December 30, 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161230070602/http://www.nba.com/gamenotes/suns.pdf |archive-date=December 30, 2016 }}</ref> On March 3, 2017, against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], Barbosa made his 544th appearance in a Suns jersey, passing [[Mark West (basketball)|Mark West]] for ninth all-time in games played. Barbosa's 14 points also pushed him past [[Connie Hawkins]] for 14th in all-time scoring with Phoenix.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cunningham|first=Cody|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/postgame/suns-battle-out-win-against-thunder-mccoy-roh-night|title=Suns Battle Out Win Against Thunder on McCoy ROH Night|work=NBA.com|date=March 3, 2017|access-date=March 5, 2017}}</ref> Barbosa's final game in his NBA career was played on March 24, in a 120–130 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]], where he recorded 11 points, five rebounds, and a steal.

On July 3, 2017, Barbosa was waived by the Suns.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/leandro-barbosa-waived-by-suns/|title=Leandro Barbosa: Waived by Suns|work=cbssports.com|date=July 3, 2017|access-date=July 3, 2017}}</ref>

===Franca Basquetebol Clube (2017–2018)===
On November 17, 2017, Barbosa returned to Brazil and signed with Franca.<ref>{{cite web|title=LEANDRINHO É FRANCA|url=https://lnb.com.br/noticias/leandrinho-e-franca/|website=lnb.com.br|access-date=November 17, 2017|date=November 17, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Franca Basquete signs Leandro Barbosa|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/america/brazil/254460/franca-basquete-signs-leandro-barbosa.html|date=November 18, 2017|access-date=November 18, 2017}}</ref>

===Minas Storm Basquete (2018–2020)===
On December 13, 2018, Barbosa signed with [[Minas Tênis Clube (basketball)|Minas]].<ref name="minas01">{{cite web| url = https://www.mg.superesportes.com.br/app/noticias/basquete/2018/12/13/noticia_basquete,556535/minas-acerta-contratacao-de-leandrinho.shtml | title = Minas acerta contratação de Leandrinho| trans-title = Minas signs Leandrinho | publisher = [[Superesportes]] | author = Ivan Drummond | date = 2018-12-13 | access-date = 2018-12-13}}</ref> In the 2019–20 season, he was the league's leading scorer at 20.1 points per game before the season shut down due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. Barbosa and his then-pregnant wife contracted the virus, but they both recovered.<ref>{{cite news|title=Leandro Barbosa's Family Grew During the Pandemic|newspaper=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/04/27/sports/basketball/leandro-barbosa.html|date=April 27, 2020|last1=Stein|first1=Marc}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On September 14, 2020, Barbosa announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite web|title=Leandro Barbosa Announces Retirement, Joins Warriors as Player Mentor Coach|website=[[Bleacher Report]] |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2909108-leandro-barbosa-announces-retirement-joins-warriors-as-player-mentor-coach|date=September 14, 2020}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On September 14, 2020, the [[Golden State Warriors]] announced that Barbosa would return as a player mentor coach.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news-blogs/leandro-barbosa-20200914|title=Warriors Name Leandro Barbosa Player Mentor Coach 14-Year NBA Veteran & 2015 NBA Champion Joins Head Coach Steve Kerr's Staff|date=September 14, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 14, 2020}}</ref> He won his second [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] after the Warriors defeated the [[Boston Celtics]] in six games during the [[2022 NBA Finals]].

On August 12, 2022, Barbosa was hired by the [[Sacramento Kings]] as an assistant coach.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kings Announce Coaching Staff for 2022-23 Season |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-coaching-staff-for-2022-23-season |website=NBA.com |date=August 12, 2022}}</ref>

==National team career==
Barbosa was a longtime member of the senior [[Brazilian national basketball team]]. With Brazil, he played at the following major tournaments: the [[2002 FIBA World Cup]], the [[2003 FIBA AmeriCup]], the [[2005 FIBA AmeriCup]], the [[2006 FIBA World Cup]], the [[2007 FIBA AmeriCup]], the [[2009 FIBA AmeriCup]], the [[2010 FIBA World Cup]], the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]], the [[2014 FIBA World Cup]], and the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20170330212451/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp/q/Leandro%20Barbosa/pid/_/players.html Leandro BARBOSA (BRA) SENIOR LEVEL.]</ref>

Barbosa was the [[FIBA AmeriCup Top Scorer|top scorer]] of the 2007 FIBA AmeriCup.

==Personal life==
Barbosa lived with Brazilian actress [[Samara Felippo]] from 2008 to 2013. They have two daughters, born in 2009<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ego.globo.com/Gente/Noticias/0,,MUL1633398-9798,00-SAMARA+FELIPPO+SE+SEPARA+DE+LEANDRINHO.html|title=Samara Felippo se separa de Leandrinho|language=pt|publisher=[[Rede Globo|G1 – EGO]]|date=December 1, 2010|access-date=December 6, 2010|archive-date=July 3, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130703182019/http://ego.globo.com/Gente/Noticias/0,,MUL1633398-9798,00-SAMARA+FELIPPO+SE+SEPARA+DE+LEANDRINHO.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://celebridades.uol.com.br/noticias/redacao/2011/06/01/samara-felippo-e-leandrinho-reatam-relacao-e-vao-juntos-ao-fashion-rio.htm|title=Samara Felippo e Leandrinho reatam relação e vão juntos ao Fashion Rio|publisher=[[Universo Online|UOL]]|date=June 1, 2011|access-date=December 26, 2011}}</ref> and 2013.

Barbosa is married to the international top model Talita Rocca. The ceremony was held in Brazil on July 6, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://vogue.globo.com/beleza/gente/noticia/2019/04/jogador-de-basquete-leandrinho-vai-casar-com-modelo-lista-tem-convidados-famosos.html|title=Jogador de basquete Leandrinho vai casar com modelo; lista tem convidados famosos|website=vogue.globo.com|date=April 30, 2019 |access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref>
